markers.caveat: Most common in people with Armenian, Turkish, Arab, Jewish or other Mediterranean ancestry.

verify.note: Not on the AncestryDNA chip; 23andMe coverage unconfirmed.

markers.about: MEFV makes pyrin, which controls inflammation. M694V is the main severe variant behind familial Mediterranean fever, with fever attacks treated by colchicine.

markers.name: Gilbert syndrome (UGT1A1)

CC.text: No copies of the Gilbert syndrome version.

CT.text: One copy of the Gilbert syndrome version. This usually has no effect.

TT.text: Two copies: you likely have Gilbert syndrome, a harmless condition in about 1 in 10 people. Bilirubin (a yellow substance in blood) can read high on blood tests, and your eyes may look slightly yellow when you are ill, tired or fasting. Tell your doctor so it is not mistaken for liver disease. It also affects the dose of a few drugs, such as the cancer drug irinotecan.

markers.caveat: This marker stands in for the UGT1A1*28 version, which DNA chips cannot read directly.

verify.note: Proxy (tag) for UGT1A1*28; strongest in people of European ancestry.

markers.about: UGT1A1 clears bilirubin. Two copies of this weaker version cause Gilbert syndrome, a harmless mild yellowing when ill or fasting; it also affects irinotecan.

markers.name: HLA-B27 (proxy marker)

GG.text: The proxy marker shows no sign of HLA-B27.

AG.text: The proxy marker suggests you carry HLA-B27. About 1 in 12 people of European ancestry do, and most never have problems. It is linked to ankylosing spondylitis: long-lasting back pain and stiffness, often worse in the morning. If you have that kind of back pain, mention this result to your doctor.

AA.text: The proxy marker suggests you carry HLA-B27 (possibly two copies). Most people with it never have problems. If you have long-lasting back pain and stiffness, mention this result to your doctor.

markers.caveat: A proxy that works best in people of European ancestry; a blood test can confirm HLA-B27.

verify.note: Proxy (tag) accuracy varies by ancestry.

markers.about: HLA-B27 is linked to ankylosing spondylitis and some eye and joint inflammation, but most of the 8% of Europeans who have it never develop these. This is a stand-in marker.

markers.name: Iron levels, TMPRSS6

GG.text: No copies of the version linked to slightly lower iron levels.

AG.text: One copy of a common version linked to slightly lower iron and hemoglobin levels. Small effect.

AA.text: Two copies; slightly lower iron and hemoglobin levels on average. Diet, blood loss and periods matter far more.

markers.caveat: Small effect.

verify.note: Effect allele from published studies; needs review.

markers.about: TMPRSS6 helps turn down hepcidin, the hormone that limits iron absorption. This common variant slightly lowers iron and hemoglobin but rarely causes anemia.

markers.name: NUDT15 (thiopurine sensitivity)

CC.text: No copies of this thiopurine-sensitivity variant.

CT.text: One copy: thiopurine drugs (azathioprine, mercaptopurine) may need lower doses. Tell prescribers.

TT.text: Two copies: very high risk of serious side effects from thiopurine drugs at standard doses. Tell prescribers.

markers.caveat: Most common in people of East Asian or Hispanic ancestry.

verify.note: Not on the AncestryDNA chip; 23andMe coverage unconfirmed.

markers.about: NUDT15 also helps clear thiopurine drugs. This very weak version, common in East Asian and Hispanic ancestry, can cause dangerous drops in white blood cells at standard doses.

markers.name: CYP4F2*3 (warfarin dose)

CC.text: No copies of this version.

CT.text: One copy: warfarin may need a slightly higher dose. Mention it to prescribers.

TT.text: Two copies: warfarin often needs a somewhat higher dose. Mention it to prescribers.

markers.caveat: A small effect compared with VKORC1 and CYP2C9.
markers.about: CYP4F2 clears vitamin K. The slower *3 version leaves more vitamin K, so slightly more warfarin is needed; the effect is smaller than VKORC1 or CYP2C9.

markers.name: HLA-A*31:01 proxy (carbamazepine reaction)

AA.text: The proxy marker shows no sign of HLA-A*31:01.

AT.text: The proxy marker suggests HLA-A*31:01 may be present. It raises the risk of a serious skin reaction to carbamazepine, an epilepsy and nerve-pain drug. A clinical HLA test can confirm; tell prescribers.

TT.text: The proxy marker suggests HLA-A*31:01 may be present (possibly two copies). It raises the risk of a serious skin reaction to carbamazepine. A clinical HLA test can confirm; tell prescribers.

markers.caveat: A proxy that works best in people of European ancestry.

verify.note: A/T marker and proxy; accuracy varies by ancestry.

markers.about: HLA-A*31:01 is linked to serious skin reactions to carbamazepine. This marker usually travels with it in Europeans, but only a direct HLA test is reliable.

markers.name: CYP2B6*6 (efavirenz)

GG.text: No copies of the slower CYP2B6 version.

GT.text: One copy of a slower version: the HIV drug efavirenz (and some others, such as methadone) may build up somewhat. Mention it to prescribers.

TT.text: Two copies: slow processing of efavirenz. Standard doses can cause side effects such as dizziness and vivid dreams; a lower dose may be needed. Tell prescribers.

markers.caveat: CYP2B6*6 is defined by two markers; this checks the main one.
markers.about: CYP2B6 clears the HIV drug efavirenz. The slower *6 version lets it build up, causing dizziness or vivid dreams; guidelines lower the dose for slow processors.

markers.name: IFNL3 (hepatitis C)

CC.text: The version linked to clearing hepatitis C more often, both on its own and with older interferon treatment.

CT.text: One copy of each version. This mainly mattered for older hepatitis C treatment.

TT.text: The version linked to clearing hepatitis C less often with older interferon treatment. Modern hepatitis C pills work well regardless.

markers.caveat: Mostly of historical interest: today's hepatitis C pills cure most people whatever this result.

verify.note: Weak current relevance; included for completeness.

markers.about: This immune-gene marker once predicted whether interferon would cure hepatitis C. Modern pills cure most people regardless, so it now matters little.

markers.name: Omega-3 and omega-6 fats

CC.text: Your body likely turns plant omega-3 and omega-6 fats into the long-chain forms efficiently.

CT.text: One copy of a version that turns plant fats into long-chain omega-3 and omega-6 fats a bit less efficiently.

TT.text: Two copies: your body likely makes long-chain omega-3 fats (the kind in fish) from plant sources less efficiently, so eating fish or other direct sources may matter more for you.

markers.caveat: Diet affects these levels more than this gene.

verify.note: New trait marker; effect direction from published studies, needs review.

markers.about: FADS1 turns plant omega-3 and omega-6 fats into longer forms. This less efficient version makes direct sources such as fish more important.

markers.name: Making vitamin A from beta-carotene (marker 1)

CC.text: Typical conversion of beta-carotene (in carrots and sweet potatoes) into vitamin A.

CT.text: One copy of a version that turns beta-carotene into vitamin A somewhat less efficiently.

TT.text: Two copies: somewhat less efficient conversion of beta-carotene into vitamin A. Eggs, dairy and fish provide vitamin A directly.

markers.caveat: Rarely matters with a varied diet.

verify.note: New trait marker; effect direction from published studies, needs review.

markers.about: BCO1 turns plant beta-carotene into vitamin A. This variant lowers its efficiency, which rarely matters if you eat dairy, eggs or fish.

markers.name: Making vitamin A from beta-carotene (marker 2)

AA.text: Typical conversion of beta-carotene into vitamin A.

AT.text: One copy of a version that turns beta-carotene into vitamin A somewhat less efficiently.

TT.text: Two copies: somewhat less efficient conversion of beta-carotene into vitamin A. Eggs, dairy and fish provide vitamin A directly.

markers.caveat: Rarely matters with a varied diet.

verify.note: New trait marker; effect direction from published studies, needs review.

markers.about: A second BCO1 variant that lowers beta-carotene to vitamin A conversion; it rarely matters with some animal foods.

markers.name: Saturated fat and weight

AA.text: No copies of the version linked to weight gain on diets high in saturated fat.

AG.text: One copy; no clear effect.

GG.text: Two copies of a version linked in some studies to more weight gain when eating a lot of saturated fat (butter, fatty meat). Other studies did not find this.

markers.caveat: Weak, inconsistent evidence. Do not change your diet because of this result alone.

verify.note: New trait marker; effect direction from published studies, needs review.

markers.about: APOA2 is an HDL protein. People with two copies of this variant gained more weight on high saturated-fat diets in several studies; the effect is modest.

markers.name: Straight or curly hair

AA.text: The most common version. Your hair type depends mostly on other genes.

AT.text: One copy of a version linked to straighter hair in people of European ancestry.

TT.text: Two copies of a version linked to straighter hair in people of European ancestry.

markers.caveat: It nudges hair toward straight but does not decide it.

verify.note: New trait marker; effect direction from published studies, needs review.

markers.about: TCHH stiffens the inner hair follicle. This variant is linked to straighter hair in Europeans but explains little of hair shape.

markers.name: Hair loss with age (mostly men), marker 1

GG.text: No copies of the version linked to male pattern hair loss.

AG.text: One copy of a version linked to a higher chance of male pattern hair loss.

AA.text: Two copies of a version linked to a higher chance of male pattern hair loss.

composites.name: Warfarin sensitivity (VKORC1, CYP2C9 and CYP4F2 together)
texts: Typical warfarin sensitivity: the usual starting doses are expected to fit. Based on VKORC1 GG and CYP2C9 *1/*1 (the FDA warfarin label table). This only matters if you are ever prescribed warfarin, a blood thinner.

composites.about: Warfarin guidelines combine VKORC1, CYP2C9 and CYP4F2 to estimate sensitivity; together they explain about a third of dose differences.

composites.name: Hair loss, both genes together
texts: No risk versions at either hair-loss gene: lower odds of male-pattern hair loss, though many other genes play a part.
A risk version at one of the two hair-loss genes (AR): somewhat higher odds of male-pattern hair loss.
A risk version at one of the two hair-loss genes (20p11): somewhat higher odds of male-pattern hair loss.

Risk versions at both hair-loss genes. In one study, men with risk versions at both had about 7 times the odds of male-pattern hair loss; about 1 in 7 men have this combination. The effect in women is much smaller.
composites.caveat: Based on Richards et al. 2008 (Nature Genetics). AR is on the X chromosome, inherited from the mother.

composites.name: Vitamin A from beta-carotene, both markers together
texts: Neither version was found: a typical ability to make vitamin A from beta-carotene.
One version (R267S) with a small effect on its own. A normal varied diet covers this.
One version linked to slower conversion (A379V). In a small study of women, this alone meant about 32% less vitamin A made from beta-carotene. A normal varied diet covers this.

Both versions linked to slower conversion. In a small study, women with both made about 69% less vitamin A from a dose of beta-carotene. If you eat little meat, eggs, fish or dairy, do not rely on carrots and other orange vegetables alone for vitamin A.
composites.caveat: Based on Leung et al. 2009, a small study of women.

variants.name: ABCA4
variants.note: One copy of a harmful variant in ABCA4, a gene for the light-sensing cells of the eye. ABCA4 conditions, such as Stargardt disease (a cause of central vision loss), are recessive: they happen only when both copies of the gene carry a harmful variant. With one copy you are a carrier and usually have no symptoms. It matters for children if a partner also carries an ABCA4 variant.
variants.about: ABCA4 clears vitamin A byproducts in the retina. Harmful variants in both copies cause Stargardt disease.

variants.name: GAA c.-32-13T>G
variants.note: One copy of the most common variant behind late-onset Pompe disease, a slowly progressing muscle condition. Pompe disease is recessive, so one copy makes you a carrier, usually with no symptoms. It matters for children if a partner is also a carrier.
conditions: Glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, late-onset
variants.about: GAA breaks down stored glycogen. Harmful variants in both copies cause Pompe disease, which weakens muscles.

variants.name: GJB2 M34T
variants.note: One copy of a mild GJB2 hearing-loss variant. GJB2 hearing loss is recessive: people with two variants typically have mild to moderate hearing loss, and some have none. With one copy you are a carrier.
variants.about: GJB2 makes connexin 26, needed for hearing. Harmful variants in both copies are the most common cause of inherited hearing loss.

variants.name: GJB2 V37I
variants.note: One copy of a mild GJB2 hearing-loss variant that is common in people of East Asian ancestry. GJB2 hearing loss is recessive: people with two variants typically have mild to moderate hearing loss, and some have none. With one copy you are a carrier.
conditions: Knuckle pads, deafness AND leukonychia syndrome
variants.about: GJB2 makes connexin 26, needed for hearing. Harmful variants in both copies are the most common cause of inherited hearing loss.

variants.name: PMM2 R141H
variants.note: One copy of the most common variant behind PMM2-CDG, a rare inherited metabolic condition that appears in early childhood. It is recessive, so one copy makes you a carrier with no symptoms. Roughly 1 in 60 to 1 in 220 people of European ancestry carry it.
variants.about: PMM2 helps attach sugar chains to proteins. Harmful variants in both copies cause PMM2-CDG, which affects development.

variants.name: VWF R854Q
variants.note: One copy of R854Q, the most common cause of type 2N von Willebrand disease, a mild bleeding disorder. Bleeding problems usually happen only with two copies, or together with another VWF variant; one copy usually causes none. Mention it to your doctor if you or relatives have unusual bleeding, or before surgery.
variants.about: VWF helps platelets stick. Variants can cause von Willebrand disease, the most common inherited bleeding disorder.
